{{Short description|Chinese academic and administrator (born 1958)}}
{{family name hatnote|[[Zhang (surname)|Zhang]]|lang=Chinese}}

'''Zhang Jie''' ({{zh|s=张杰}}; born January 31, 1958) is a Chinese [[physicist]]. He served as President of [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]] from November 2006 to February 2017.<ref>{{cite news |date=2017-02-24 |title= |script-title=zh:中共中央国务院决定林忠钦任上海交大校长 |trans-title=The Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party decided that Lin Zhongqin should become the president of Shanghai Jiaotong University |url=http://newspaper.jfdaily.com/jfrb/html/2017-02/24/content_10723.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170224131944/http://newspaper.jfdaily.com/jfrb/html/2017-02/24/content_10723.htm |archive-date=2017-02-24 |language=zh}}</ref> 

==Upbringing and education==
Zhang Jie was born in 1958 in [[Taiyuan]], [[Shanxi]], China. He received both his bachelor's degree and master's degree from [[Inner Mongolia University]], and his Ph.D. degree from the [[Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS) in 1988. 

==Career==
From 1988 to 1998, he was a visiting scholar at the [[Max Planck Society]] in Germany and at [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory]] in the United Kingdom. In 1999, he returned to China and worked as a research scientist at the CAS. He was appointed head of Bureau of Fundamental Science at the CAS in 2003. On November 27, 2006, Zhang replaced [[Xie Shengwu]] as President of [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]].{{cn|date=January 2025}}

Zhang Jie is a member of the Board of Trustees of [[King Abdullah University of Science and Technology]] (KAUST).<ref>[http://www.kaust.edu.sa/about/board-trustees.aspx Board of Trustees of KAUST] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090421031605/http://www.kaust.edu.sa/about/board-trustees.aspx |date=2009-04-21}}</ref>

Zhang Jie was an alternate of the [[17th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party|17th]] and [[18th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party]].{{cn|date=January 2025}}

==Awards and honors==
He was elected a member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 2003. He was elected to the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] on March 28, 2007. He was elected as foreign associate of the US [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2012_05_01_NAS_Election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120504002407/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2012_05_01_NAS_Election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 4, 2012|title=National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|date=2012-05-01|access-date=2019-11-23}}</ref> In 2022, he became a laureate of the [[Asian Scientist 100]] by the ''[[Asian Scientist]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.asianscientist.com/as100/ |title=The Asian Scientist 100 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= |publisher= [[Asian Scientist]] |access-date= 13 March 2025 |quote= |language= }}</ref>
